name: TeamStarWolf - Hugging Face AI Supply Chain (Enterprise)
description: Enterprise ATT&CK v20.0 techniques bound in the Hugging Face case study. Score 100: an ATLAS-published ATT&CK reference on a technique ATLAS maps in a Hugging Face case study, or an ATT&CK procedure that names Hugging Face (S9035). Score 50: the study's own inference, labelled Inferred in its comment. Comments carry the study's source numbers.

50: analyst inference, labelled in the comment

techniques.comment: ATLAS bridge: AML.T0010 carries ATT&CK reference T1195. Used directly by AML.CS0031 (nullifAI, published 2025-02-06). Sources: [65]; [30]; [69].
ATLAS bridge: AML.T0021 maps to T1585. AML.CS0027 (2023-08-23), AML.CS0065 (2025-09-03). Sources: [65]; [34].
ATLAS bridge: AML.T0073 maps to T1684.001. AML.CS0027 organization confusion (2023-08-23). Sources: [65]; [68].
ATLAS bridge: AML.T0074 maps to T1036. AML.CS0027 (training.bin), AML.CS0065 (recreated namespace). Sources: [65]; [68]; [34].
ATLAS bridge: AML.T0055 maps to T1552. AML.CS0027 (2023) and AML.CS0068 S16 (HF tokens exposed in a public dataset, 2026-07-10), S21, S27, S32 (2026-07-11). Sources: [65]; [41]; [43].
ATLAS bridge: AML.T0012 maps to T1078. AML.CS0068 S17 (2026-07-10 to 07-11) and S33 (2026-07-11). Sources: [65]; [41].
ATLAS bridge: AML.T0105 maps to T1611. AML.CS0068 S31, privileged pod to node root (2026-07-11). Sources: [65]; [41].
ATLAS bridge: AML.T0091.000 maps to T1550.001. AML.CS0068 S28 and S34 (2026-07-11). Sources: [65]; [41].
ATT&CK S9035 LAMEHUG procedure: Hugging Face API used to query Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct for Windows commands. Source: [71].
ATLAS bridge: AML.T0036 maps to T1213. AML.CS0068 S35: internal MongoDB, four private source repositories, five customer datasets (2026-07-11 to 07-13). Sources: [65]; [41].
ATLAS bridge: AML.T0050 maps to T1059. AML.CS0068 S09 (harness, 2026-07-09) and S24 (Jinja2 path in the Dataset Server pod, 2026-07-11). Sources: [65]; [41].
ATLAS bridge: AML.T0122 maps to T1210. AML.CS0068 S02: the Artifactory SSRF crosses the evaluation network boundary (evaluation period, no day given). Sources: [65]; [41]; [42].
ATLAS bridge: AML.T0095 maps to T1593. AML.CS0065 S00: Unit 42 reviewed public catalogs, author pages and repositories for deleted namespaces (2025-09-03). Sources: [65]; [34].

ATLAS bridge: AML.T0123 maps to T1027. AML.CS0068 S14 and S26, chunked, compressed, Base64 and XOR-encoded traffic (2026-07-09 to 07-13). Inferred: nullifAI used 7z compression and a deliberately broken pickle stream so Picklescan did not flag the payload (2025). Sources: [65]; [41]; [30]; [79].

ATLAS bridge: AML.T0049 maps to T1190. AML.CS0068 S08, the exposed code-evaluation harness (2026-07-09). Inferred: the malicious dataset against the public dataset-processing service (2026-07-11), since AML.T0119 has no ATT&CK reference. Sources: [65]; [40]; [41].
ATLAS bridge: AML.T0037 maps to T1005. AML.CS0068 S20, the HDF5 external-storage read returned the pod environment and worker source (2026-07-11). Sources: [65]; [41].
Inferred: models pulled by name from a hub, namespace reuse (Unit 42, 2025-09-03) and malicious uploads (JFrog, 2024-02-27). ATT&CK does not name model hubs. Sources: [69]; [75]; [27]; [34].
Inferred: malicious models uploaded to the Hub (JFrog 2024-02-27; nullifAI 2025). AML.T0115.001 has no ATT&CK reference. Sources: [70]; [27]; [30]; [65].
Inferred: a user loads a pickle-bearing model (JFrog 2024; nullifAI 2025). AML.T0011 has no ATT&CK reference. Sources: [69]; [27]; [30]; [65].
Inferred: pickle __reduce__ payloads run Python when a model is loaded (JFrog 2024-02-27). Sources: [27]; [8].
Inferred: PoisonGPT uploaded as EleuterAI, the real name with one letter removed (2023-07-09). Sources: [67]; [79].
Inferred: crafted model files that exploit loader bugs, such as llama.cpp GGUF heap overflows (2024) and Keras safe_mode bypasses. Sources: [57]; [58]; [60].
Inferred: 1,681 valid HF tokens found on GitHub and the Hub (Lasso, 2023-12-04). Source: [25].
Inferred: Lasso found the tokens by regex code search of GitHub and the Hub (2023-12-04). Source: [25].
